description: I’m passionate about Earth observation, remote sensing, and building real-world applications that make complex satellite data accessible and actionable. I find the power of Radar imagery—peering through clouds and night skies to track environmental changes—incredibly exciting!
summary:
SPHEREx Sky Explorer is a public-facing web tool that makes it easier for anyone to explore changes in the infrared sky over time. Users can enter Right Ascension and Declination coordinates, select a known astronomical target or a custom sky position, and compare multiple observations of the same region.

The tool provides simple visual modes including time-series images, blink comparison, and difference images, helping users identify objects that move or change brightness. The project is designed as an accessible starting point for exploring SPHEREx data and supporting the search for moving and variable astronomical objects such as asteroids, comets, brown dwarfs, and variable stars.

The prototype is built with Python and Streamlit, with a separate astronomy/data-processing layer that can be connected to real SPHEREx archive imagery and future data releases.
details:
What problem are we solving?

SPHEREx repeatedly maps the sky in infrared wavelengths, creating a large amount of time-dependent astronomical information. Objects can reveal themselves by moving or changing brightness between observations, but manually comparing large numbers of images is difficult.

Our project addresses this problem by providing a simple interface where users can select a region of the sky and quickly compare observations from different times.

How does it work?

The user starts by entering a sky position using Right Ascension and Declination or selecting one of the example targets included in the application.

The application then provides controls for:

  • Sky coordinates
  • Field of view
  • Number of observations
  • Display mode
  • Target selection

Users can view the observations as a sequence of images, move between observations in Blink mode, or compare two observations using a Difference image.

A brightness analysis also provides a simple view of how the selected field changes over time.

Example targets

The prototype includes example coordinates for:

  • WISE 0855
  • Barnard's Star
  • Epsilon Indi B
  • RW Aurigae
  • R Draconis

WISE 0855 is included using the challenge-provided coordinates:

RA: 08h55m10.831s
Declination: -07d14m42.53s

NASA data connection

The project is designed around SPHEREx data and provides a dedicated data-access layer so that official SPHEREx imagery and future data releases can be integrated without rebuilding the user interface.

The current prototype includes a demonstration image generator for development and interface testing. These generated images are not presented as actual SPHEREx observations.

The next step is to connect the data layer directly to the appropriate public SPHEREx archive products.

Technology

The application uses:

  • Python
  • Streamlit
  • NumPy
  • Astropy
  • Requests
  • Pillow
  • Plotly

The project is separated into a web interface (webtool.py) and an astronomy/data-processing layer (spherex_api.py).

Why is this useful?

The goal is to lower the barrier to participating in astronomical discovery. Instead of requiring users to understand complex astronomical data-processing pipelines, the tool gives them a visual workflow:

Coordinate → Observations → Comparison → Change detection → Potential discovery

The same interface can eventually be expanded with real SPHEREx imagery, infrared bands, spectra, catalog overlays, and automated motion detection.

Future development

Planned improvements include:

  • Integration with official SPHEREx imagery
  • FITS and WCS support
  • Exploration of SPHEREx's infrared bands
  • On-the-fly spectra
  • Automatic moving-object detection
  • Gaia and WISE catalog overlays
  • Direct coordinate-based URLs
  • Additional metadata and contamination information

The project is intended to grow as new SPHEREx data releases become available.
